title: Gender-Affirming Surgery: Chest, Vaginoplasty and Phalloplasty

steps.say: Small chests with minimal excess tissue are suiting a scar-concealing minimal approach. Semicircular or concentric periareolar incisions at the areolar border are removing gland and tightening mild laxity. Scars are hiding in the pigment transition while the chest flattens.
steps.tx: **Chest masculinization** top surgery for minimal tissue uses semicircular or periareolar concentric **incisions** at the areolar border. Small volumes leave through the same opening that tightens mild laxity. Scars hide in the pigment transition while the chest flattens. Mild laxity tightens through the same opening without extra scars.

steps.say: Drooping larger chests are needing the workhorse double-incision operation. Transverse chest incisions are removing the breast while free grafts are replacing the nipples higher. A flat masculine contour with pectoral-line scars is emerging from this single stage.
steps.tx: **Double incision mastectomy** with **free nipple grafting** is the workhorse for moderate to **severe ptosis**. Transverse incisions remove the breast while grafted nipples resurface higher. Flat masculine contour replaces droop, with scars fading along the pectoral lines over months. Drains stay until output falls to safe levels.

steps.say: Nipple size and position are declaring male versus female chest at a glance. A smaller oval complex of twenty two to twenty eight millimetres is sitting lateral and low over the pectoral edge. Placement near the fourth interspace is completing the masculine read.
steps.tx: The **male NAC** is smaller at **22 to 28 mm** diameter, oval, and placed lateral and inferior over the **pectoralis major** edge near the **fourth intercostal space**. Size with position reads male at a glance. Grafts are sized and sited to this template.

rows: Twenty two to twenty eight millimetres

steps.say: A functional vulva with vaginal depth is arising from inverted natal tissue. Penile skin flaps turned inside out are lining a cavity dissected between rectum and prostate. Scrotal grafts are adding depth where penile skin alone falls short of the goal.
steps.tx: **Penile inversion vaginoplasty**, the gold standard transfeminine operation, builds a **neovaginal cavity** between rectum and prostate from inverted penile skin flaps. Scrotal grafts add depth. The cavity lines with skin that tolerates the dilation protocol from the very start. Depth maintenance decides long-term functional success.

The image shows a side view of the pelvis with a skin lined cavity dissected between rectum and prostate, extended by scrotal graft. This is **penile inversion vaginoplasty**, creating a **neovaginal cavity** from inverted skin flaps. Added graft depth plus lifelong **dilation** protocol decides functional success.
steps.say: The picture shows the pelvis in profile with a new cavity lined by inverted skin between rectum and prostate, with extra graft at the tip. It teaches the gold standard cavity construction where skin lines the space and graft adds depth. Keeping depth with regular dilation decides long term function.

steps.say: Erotic sensation is surviving the transformation by careful pedicle preservation. The glans reduced in bulk is remaining attached to its dorsal neurovascular bundle. Blood supply with sensory innervation is reaching the neoclitoris under its new hood.
steps.tx: The **neoclitoris** comes from the **glans penis** left pedicled on the **dorsal neurovascular bundle**. Erotic sensory innervation with vascularity survives the transfer. Bulk reduces to clitoral size while feeling stays rooted in the original nerve supply for life. Hood construction shelters the sensitive tip from direct friction.

steps.say: A sensate phallus with a built-in urethra is rolling from forearm skin in one stage. An inner skin tube for urine is wrapping inside an outer tube for the shaft. Microvascular transplantation is keeping this double construction alive in its new position.
steps.tx: **Phalloplasty** most often uses the microvascular **radial forearm** free flap in a **tube-within-a-tube** design: an inner tube forms the urethra inside an outer shaft tube. One stage yields a standing phallus with a working urinary conduit together. The forearm scar is the price of reliability.

The image shows a forearm flap rolled as an inner urethra tube nested inside an outer shaft tube, with radial artery and vein pedicles for connection. This is **phalloplasty** by microvascular **radial forearm** flap in a **tube within a tube** design. One stage yields a standing phallus with a working urinary conduit.
steps.say: The picture shows an inner urine tube inside an outer shaft tube with artery and vein ready for joining. It teaches the forearm free flap option where one operation builds both shaft and conduit together. The visible vessels explain why microsurgery keeps the double construction alive.

vis.alt: Rolled flap with inner urine tube inside outer shaft tube and vessels shown.
vis.caption: Nested tube construction for phallus with conduit Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.say: Forearm scars or thin radial tissue are shifting the plan to the thigh. The anterolateral thigh flap with its hidden donor scar is serving as the primary alternative. Thicker fat is challenging urethral rolling, so heavier patients are counselling toward staged urethral work.
steps.tx: **ALT phalloplasty** uses the **anterolateral thigh** flap as the primary **alternative** donor when forearm tissue fails or is declined. Abundant tissue hides its scar well. Thicker fat challenges **tube** rolling, so staging the urethral connection suits heavier patients better. Sensation develops as nerves regenerate into the flap over months.

steps.say: Irreversible genital operations are never proceeding on surgical enthusiasm alone. Version eight of the WPATH standards is requiring mental health, endocrine, and surgical evaluations beforehand. Persistent dysphoria with capacity and realistic expectations is opening the path to the theatre.
steps.tx: Before irreversible genital surgery, **version 8** of the **WPATH Standards of Care** sends every patient through mental health, endocrine, and surgical review. Persistent dysphoria, controlled comorbidity, capacity, and realistic expectations open the path. Careful gatekeeping protects patients and surgeons alike from regret and reoperation.
